# 04b The `:::` shorthand works inside an edge line too

## Outcome

`A[Start]:::hot --> B[End]` and `A:::hot --> B` parse and apply the definition, as they do in
Mermaid. The shorthand works wherever a node can be written, not only on a line of its own.

## Why this ticket exists

Measured, not assumed:

```
A[Start]:::hot          ok
A[Start]:::hot --> B    REJECTED  ("Unrecognized flowchart line")
A:::hot --> B           REJECTED
```

Both rejected forms are valid Mermaid. Ticket 04 delivered the shorthand at the node declaration
and deliberately did not touch `EDGE_RE`, because widening it was outside its criteria — the right
call there, and the reason this is a ticket rather than a silent extension.

The repo owner has since made Mermaid compatibility an absolute condition: **a document that
renders in Mermaid must render here.** This is the same shape of gap board 1 closed when
`flowchart TB` was rejected — caused by implementation order, not by anyone's design decision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `A[Start]:::hot --> B[End]` parses: both endpoints are declared with their labels, and `A`
      carries the definition.
- [x] `A:::hot --> B` parses: the bare form applies without claiming a label, exactly as ticket 04
      established for the standalone form. `A --> B[End]` followed by `B:::hot --> C` must keep
      `End` and raise no redeclaration warning.
- [x] The shorthand works on **either** endpoint, and on both at once:
      `A:::hot --> B:::cold`. Assert all three positions.
- [x] A `:::` naming a definition no `classDef` defines is the existing error, reported once per
      occurrence, with the `authoredAs: ":::"` spelling ticket 04 established.
- [x] Chained edges are out of scope and stay rejected — `A --> B --> C` is a separate
      compatibility gap on the next board's list, and this ticket must not half-implement it. Pin
      that it is still an unrecognized line, so the boundary is visible.
- [x] Every existing flowchart parser test passes **unedited**. This widens what is accepted; it
      changes nothing that already parsed.
